case_content.title: Prompt #1 - Juice Producer
case_content.content: A major producer of juice processes and packages fruit juice for retail outlets. Traditionally, the producer packaged the juice in 18-ounce carton containers. Recently, in response to market demand, the producer purchased a machine that packages the juice in plastic gallons of 36 ounces. Over the next couple of years, sales continued to grow by an average of 20% per year. However, as sales increased, profits steadily decreased. The owner does not understand why and has hired you to help identify the issue.

case_content.title: Interviewer Guidance - Prompt #1
case_content.content:
High Level Plan of Attack:

• Sales have been increasing, so revenue is probably not the main issue.

• The problem is likely on the cost side.

• Because of the change in packaging, the producer may have incurred additional costs that were not properly accounted for, causing profits to decline.

case_content.title: Interviewer Guidance - Framework
case_content.content:
Lay Out Your Thoughts:

• Use the profitability framework.

• Gather information on both revenue and costs, but focus mainly on the cost side.

case_content.title: Expected Analysis - Revenue and Pricing
case_content.content:
Dig Deeper: Gather Facts / Make Calculations:

• How much did the producer charge for the 18-ounce carton? The producer charged $2.00 per container.

• How much did the producer charge for the 36-ounce plastic gallon? Since the gallon was twice the size, the producer wanted to provide an incentive to buy and sold it at $3.50 per gallon.

• How was the cost of the new equipment accounted for in the price? The producer raised prices across the board by $0.50 on all packages, both cartons and gallons, selling them at $2.50 and $4.00 respectively. 

• Does it cost the same to package juice in cartons as it does in gallons? No. Plastic is more expensive than the paper carton traditionally used.

• The producer also had to hire more experienced labor to operate the gallon-packaging machine because it is more complicated than the carton machine.

• The producer assumed that because demand was higher for gallons, the company would cover the additional costs through increased volume.

• What about overhead costs? All factory costs are added together and divided by the number of units produced.[ This should raise concern because the issue is now clearly related to cost allocation. The plastic gallons should carry higher costs and therefore should likely have a higher price.] 

• What percentage of sales are gallons versus cartons? As customers became more aware of the gallons, they liked them more. Plastic gallons now represent 60% of sales.

• The owner has been pleased about that.

• However, gallons cost more to package, while their price is lower on a per-ounce basis than cartons.

• The candidate should identify that the company has not performed proper cost allocation to determine which product should carry which costs.

• The key analytical insight is that the producer is selling more of the product that is underpriced relative to its true cost.

case_content.title: Key Findings
case_content.content:
Key Findings:

• The additional costs associated with plastic gallons were averaged across all units, including cartons.

• This caused a misallocation of costs and inappropriate pricing.

• Plastic gallons were priced lower than they should have been.

• As a result, the more gallons the juice producer sold, the more profit the company lost out on.

case_content.title: Final Recommendation
case_content.content: Based on your analysis, what recommendation would you give the client?

case_content.title: Interviewer Guidance - Final Recommendation
case_content.content:
• The firm should conduct a thorough activity-based costing analysis to determine the overhead and direct costs associated with each item in the product line.

• The company should then use this cost data to price each product appropriately.

• In particular, the producer should reassess the pricing of plastic gallons, since they carry higher packaging and labor costs and are currently underpriced on a cost-adjusted basis.
